**Architecture Decision Memo: QAG-1 — a staged-visibility question/answer graph substrate**

**Status:** committed. **Scope:** shared knowledge substrate for recursively decomposing AI research agents. **Reading convention:** statements carrying a page citation are source-supported; statements marked *(design inference)* are ours and are not attributed to any corpus file.

**1. Decision.** We adopt QAG-1: a directed multigraph in which questions and answers are first-class many-to-many objects, persisted as add-only CRDTs, exchanged through synchronous rounds under staged visibility, and kept consistent by runtime-computed Dung argumentation semantics. We reject the open conversational forum and no-communication as substrate architectures; both survive as evaluation controls. This memo commits to interfaces, triggers, and failure modes rather than surveying options.

**2. Alternatives.** *No inter-agent communication* is a strong baseline, not a null: across 36 configurations Zhang et al. found no multi-agent debate (MAD) method exceeding a 20% win rate over chain-of-thought (===== PDF PAGE 1 =====), and Smit et al. conclude MAD systems "do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies" such as self-consistency and ensembling (===== PDF PAGE 1 =====). A substrate that cannot beat this control at matched compute should not ship. *Open conversational forum*: Du et al.'s protocol — peer responses concatenated into each agent's context, iterated over rounds (===== PDF PAGE 4 =====) — is an unstructured forum and reports gains on arithmetic, GSM8K, biographies, MMLU, and chess. Yet full, immediate peer visibility is also the condition under which collectives fail: Lorenz et al. report social influence "strongly reduces the group's diversity … without significantly reducing its collective errors" (===== PDF PAGE 3 =====), and Choi et al. show LLM agents conform to numerically dominant groups (χ² = 164.839, p < 0.001; ===== PDF PAGE 6 =====) and to higher-intelligence agents even when outnumbered (===== PDF PAGE 7 =====). QAG-1 keeps Du's round skeleton but changes the information topology — structured objects, staged disclosure *(design inference; no corpus source manipulates visibility timing directly)*.

**3. Data model and invariants.** Nodes: Question(id, text, status, tags) and Answer(id, body, author, round, provenance). Edges: ANSWER_ADDRESSES(a→q; many-to-many, so competing answers coexist per question and one answer may address several questions), QUESTION_RELATES(q→q; refines/depends-on), ANSWER_PROVENANCE(a→a; lineage), ANSWER_CONFLICTS(a→a; a directional attack in the sense of Dung's Definition 2, AF=(AR, attacks), ===== PDF PAGE 6 =====), and TAG from a closed vocabulary. The graph shape and edge typing are *(design inference)* anchored in that definition and in Shapiro et al.'s graph CRDT. Invariants split by layer. The CRDT layer guarantees merge convergence only. The runtime enforces: (i) unique canonical IDs; (ii) endpoint existence — an edge is admitted only if both endpoints are committed, deliberately overriding the permissive semantics whereby "addArc must work even if the page at the tail of the arc has not yet been found" (===== PDF PAGE 11 =====), since invisible dangling arcs would corrupt retrieval; (iii) closed tag vocabulary; (iv) structural disjointness of edge families, so the conflict-free and admissibility definitions (===== PDF PAGE 6 =====) apply verbatim to the ANSWER_CONFLICTS subgraph, unpolluted by provenance or addressing edges.

**4. Staged visibility and protocol.** Phase 0 (commitment): each agent assigned to a question submits an independent answer before any peer answer is exposed; the runtime gates this with a visibility state machine, withholding peer content and author identity until the agent's own commitment is durable. Rounds 1..R: each agent receives prior-round answers — content and provenance, no authorship — and emits a revision as a *new* Answer node linked by ANSWER_PROVENANCE; nothing is edited in place. Termination: a cap R or a runtime convergence test over agents' latest answers per question. The skeleton replicates Du et al. — "responses from other agents are concatenated and given as context to each agent … iteratively repeat this debate procedure over multiple rounds" (===== PDF PAGE 4 =====). Staging answers Lorenz and Choi *(design inference)*; author anonymity targets Choi's intelligence-based conformity channel specifically, though it may not eliminate it.

**5. Persistence and concurrency.** Questions, answers, edges, and tags are add-only sets: growth is monotonic, so "the add-only set is a CRDT" (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====), yielding strong convergence — "correct replicas that have delivered the same updates have equivalent state" (===== PDF PAGE 4 =====). Op-based dissemination assumes causal, reliable broadcast, a stated precondition of the CmRDT constructions. Corrections, demotions, and retractions are new nodes and edges, never deletions, so history is append-only and revision auditable. What CRDTs cannot enforce — ID uniqueness, schema validity, vocabulary control, phase gating — the runtime enforces synchronously before admitting a mutation *(design inference from the CRDT convergence conditions)*.

**6. Contradiction and belief revision.** The ANSWER_CONFLICTS subgraph is a Dung argumentation framework. The runtime computes preferred extensions — "a maximal admissible set" (===== PDF PAGE 7 =====) — for credulous acceptance, letting competing answers coexist, and the grounded extension — "the least fixed point of F_AF" (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====) — for skeptical acceptance. Trigger: any mutation to a question's conflict subgraph (a new answer or conflict edge) forces recomputation over that neighborhood; previously accepted answers may be demoted, and each demotion is itself a recorded edge. Two guards: Dung's incomputability result (===== PDF PAGE 25 =====) restricts computation to a finite per-question neighborhood, and because stable extensions may fail to exist we use only preferred and grounded semantics. Answers-as-arguments and attacks-as-conflicts are *(design inference)*; the source supplies semantics, not our graph.

**7. Retrieval and ranking.** Entry by question text, tags, or QUESTION_RELATES traversal; candidates collected via ANSWER_ADDRESSES. Ranking: extension membership first (grounded over preferred-only over contested), then provenance depth — how many critique-revise cycles an answer survived — then recency. Hard constraint: the top-k for any question must span at least two independent provenance lineages when they exist, a diversity floor motivated by Lorenz's operationalization of group diversity as "the variance of estimates" (===== PDF PAGE 6 =====) and measurable via Choi's Conformity Rate and Full Conformity Ratio (===== PDF PAGE 5 =====). All ranking metadata is runtime-computed; no agent ranks its own answers. *(Ranking is design inference.)*

**8. Model versus runtime.** The model authors questions and answers; proposes ANSWER_CONFLICTS edges with a short justification — natural-language conflict is not machine-checkable without model judgment; judges semantic equivalence for convergence; generates critiques inside rounds. The runtime owns everything deterministic: CRDT merge, invariant enforcement, visibility gating, round scheduling, extension computation, retrieval, convergence testing, metric logging. It validates every mutation as an operation and trusts no model assertion about graph structure. The split mirrors the corpus's own boundary: convergence is what CRDTs prove (===== PDF PAGE 4 =====); uniqueness and schema validity are what they cannot.

**9. Reconciling the conflict.** Du reports gains under 3 agents, 2 rounds, gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (===== PDF PAGE 5 =====) with no matched-compute control, and concedes debates can converge to incorrect answers that agents confidently affirm (===== PDF PAGE 10 =====). Smit finds no protocol dominates seven datasets (Table 2, ===== PDF PAGE 5 =====) and shows rankings reverse under tuning — agreement intensity alone lifts Multi-Persona to top-performing (===== PDF PAGE 6 =====). Zhang attributes variance to task type — worse on programming, better on mathematical reasoning (===== PDF PAGE 7 =====) — finds MAD converts tokens less efficiently than self-consistency (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====), and identifies model heterogeneity as the one consistent remedy (===== PDF PAGES 11–12 =====). Three named conditions reconcile the corpus *(design inference)*: task type, compute parity, and visibility/timing of peer answers. QAG-1's commitments follow: debate is scoped per task class, evaluated at matched token budgets, staged in visibility; convergence never counts as success without the recovery test below.

**10. Evaluation plan.** Three conditions at a fixed token budget: **C1**, QAG-1 as specified; **C2**, open conversational forum with full visibility, instantiating Du's 3-agent/2-round configuration as a replication arm that must reproduce his reported accuracy to be valid; **C3**, no inter-agent communication (single agent; self-consistency permitted at matched compute). Each condition receives an equal tuning budget because Smit documents hyperparameter sensitivity. Five metric families: (1) *quality* — accuracy/F1 per benchmark with paired per-question deltas; (2) *diversity/correlation* — variance/entropy of first-round pre-visibility answers, pairwise agreement, CR/FCR; (3) *latency* — wall-clock per query, all rounds counted; (4) *token cost* — total input+output tokens per query; (5) *recovery-from-wrong-consensus* — after a wrong consensus, inject a correct minority answer and measure adoption rate and rounds-to-adoption, directly testing Du's page-10 failure mode. Falsification: QAG-1 is rejected if it fails to beat C3 at matched compute on mathematical and factuality tasks, or if its diversity and recovery metrics do not significantly exceed C2's. An optional fourth condition toggling model heterogeneity probes Zhang's remedy but lies outside this commitment.

**11. Limitations and unresolved questions.** Staged visibility is inferred from conformity evidence, not observed: no corpus source manipulates visibility timing, so C1's expected advantage over C2 is a hypothesis. Mapping natural-language disagreement to a machine-checkable ANSWER_CONFLICTS edge requires model judgment; edge quality bounds the entire revision machinery. The convergence predicate (string equality versus semantic similarity) is under-specified; we default to model-judged equivalence with runtime logging. Whether gains require model heterogeneity is untested by C1–C3. Extension computation is bounded per question; global consistency across QUESTION_RELATES chains is unaddressed. Smit's sensitivity result implies tuning sweeps whose budget this memo does not fix; token accounting counts every debate round by fiat. Finally, Choi shows agents defer to perceived higher-intelligence peers even when outnumbered; anonymity mitigates but may not close that channel.
limitations: Staged visibility is a design inference: no corpus source manipulates visibility timing directly, so the causal attribution to staging is unverified (boundary finding, packet:root).
Du et al. report confident convergence to incorrect answers (PDF PAGE 10); the design treats convergence as suspect and relies on the recovery metric, which is itself untested.
Choi et al. show conformity to perceived higher-intelligence agents even when outnumbered; author anonymity mitigates but may not eliminate this channel (packet:root counterevidence).
CRDT graph semantics permit dangling arcs; the runtime's endpoint-existence check is a deliberate override, and its interaction with concurrent additions is unproven (boundary finding, packet:root).
Dung's incomputability result (PDF PAGE 25) forces extension computation onto bounded per-question neighborhoods; global consistency is unaddressed.
Evidence is restricted to the seven-file corpus; no external validation of the debate, conformity, or CRDT claims was possible (constraint C2).
unresolved: Mapping natural-language conflict to a machine-checkable ANSWER_CONFLICTS edge requires model-level inference; the runtime only stores edges (question:raised:d92ea514b5bc7760; root packet unresolved).

Whether model heterogeneity (Zhang's Heter-MAD remedy) is necessary for gains remains untested in the three planned conditions (root packet unresolved; answer:root.05-debate-nulls-boundaries.03-c3-design-inferences).
The runtime's convergence test (string equality vs. semantic similarity) is not fully specified (root packet unresolved).
Smit et al.'s hyperparameter sensitivity implies tuning sweeps, but the evaluation budget is not fixed (root packet unresolved; question:raised:1fe8c4280c2d98e0).
Page markers quoted from Smit et al. and Zhang et al. were not independently re-verified against full texts in this dossier (question:raised:d1c06c3b4c403839).
Exact token/latency accounting rules for debate rounds, and Zhang Table 4 token-consumption numbers, remain open refinements for the cost metric (question:raised:acdafc70e274e250).
